answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The tundra report exposes the merge explicitly at each velvet. Because of that, a hostile operator who spins up 129 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 187 times the capital for one share. That is 23 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
